---
title: "Changing Temporal Organisation of Heat Events Across India"
description: "Onset, duration, persistence, and recovery periods in hourly UTCI over 1980–2024."
status: "Thesis-derived manuscript in preparation"
year: 2026
---

## Research question

Is dangerous heat only becoming more intense, or is climate change also reorganising **when heat occurs, how long events persist, and how much recovery time separates them?**

## Approach

Using hourly UTCI over India from 1980–2024, the analysis tracks first and last annual exceedances, hot-season duration, heat-event frequency and length, nighttime exposure, and breaks between events.

At each native-resolution ERA5 grid point, hourly UTCI is converted into threshold-exceedance sequences. Metrics describing the temporal organisation of those sequences are calculated year by year, and long-run trends are tested using Mann-Kendall and autocorrelation-corrected Hamed-Rao Mann-Kendall tests.

## Selected results

Large parts of India show evidence of earlier starts, later ends, longer events, or shorter recovery periods, but the patterns are strongly spatially heterogeneous. North-East India, the eastern coast, and the Indo-Gangetic Plain recur across multiple indicators and thresholds.

<figure class="research-figure">
<a href="/assets/figures/odf-slide-onset-end.png" target="_blank"><img src="/assets/figures/odf-slide-onset-end.png" alt="Original thesis-defence slide showing trends in first and last annual UTCI threshold exceedances across India."></a>
<figcaption>Thesis-defence results slide, reproduced unchanged. First-exceedance trends identify regions where the hot season is beginning earlier, while last-exceedance trends identify regions where it is ending later. The 38 °C threshold shows extensive earlier onset, while later last exceedances appear across substantial parts of India.</figcaption>
</figure>

<figure class="research-figure">
<a href="/assets/figures/odf-slide-duration-breaks.png" target="_blank"><img src="/assets/figures/odf-slide-duration-breaks.png" alt="Original thesis-defence slide showing trends in heat-event lengths and breaks between events across India."></a>
<figcaption>Thesis-defence results slide, reproduced unchanged. Mean event lengths increase across large regions, while breaks between events shrink in several areas. This separates two dimensions of changing heat risk: persistence of individual events and the recovery time available between them.</figcaption>
</figure>

<figure class="research-figure">
<a href="/assets/figures/odf-slide-nighttime.png" target="_blank"><img src="/assets/figures/odf-slide-nighttime.png" alt="Original thesis-defence slide showing trends in nighttime heat-stress exceedance and median event and break lengths."></a>
<figcaption>Thesis-defence results slide, reproduced unchanged. Nighttime heat-stress exceedance fractions increase along both coasts at lower UTCI thresholds, potentially reducing opportunities for physiological recovery.</figcaption>
</figure>

A related part of the thesis examines changing meteorological signatures of heat-stress exceedance using gridpoint-level logistic regression models.
